title: Varargs (va_start, va_arg, va_copy, va_end, x86-64 register save area) in device and lifted code
description:
Audit row(s): O-03
Source: docs/audit/2026-10-29-dialect-0.1-narrowing-audit.md

Dialect location and rule: omission: not mentioned in the dialect

Rungs blocked: 3, 4, 6, 7

Removal mechanism (0.2): Lower variadic calls to an argument block in memory, and `llvm.va_start` to a `va_list` whose register-save fields point into that block, consistent with front ends' inline va_arg expansion (or run LLVM's `expand-variadics` pass, which the spike corpus already exercises, in the normaliser).

ISA 0.8 support: Yes: memory and calls (ISA §4.1, §4.2).

Why it is a narrowing / context: NS §0, §3.1 ('all of SQLite's'). Rung 3: printf; rung 4: sqlite3_mprintf, sqlite3ErrorMsg on query paths; rungs 6, 7: printk.

title: Indirect calls in device code (R2)
description:
Audit row(s): O-01; also used by B-16, B-22, B-33
Source: docs/audit/2026-10-29-dialect-0.1-narrowing-audit.md

Dialect location and rule: omission: the call graph has direct-call edges only (§4.1); §8.1 'runs host functions natively'; no lowering for CC, R or lifted code

Rungs blocked: 4, 5, 6, 7

Removal mechanism (0.2): Candidate sets for every indirect call (C1-C5 generalised; fallback as in B-33). The device closure includes all candidates. Function-address encoding: a function's address is its comparison-link address (D15). Lowering: CC/R use a compare chain or binary search over the encodings, ending in static `call @f_k`; lifted code uses `t = lift.icmp.eq fp c_k; qbranch t ^call_k ^next` with static `lift.call`. Unbounded -> reject (decision 3 analogue).

ISA 0.8 support: Yes, no change: CC `call @f` is static (ISA §4.1); `lift.call @f` is static and `qjumpr` is intra-function (ISA §4.2). Compare-and-branch is the mechanism; an indirect-call instruction would be efficiency only.

Why it is a narrowing / context: NS §0, §3.1 taint row, §3.2 (functions are placed by a driver-controlled comparison link whose link map the device loader replicates). Rung 4: SQLite VFS, pcache, mutex, function tables; rung 5: Julia `jl_fptr_*`; rungs 6, 7: kernel ops tables. Plan risk R2. Top-ten narrowing #4.

title: Four-component budget (steps, heap, stack, depth); remove (B,0,0,0) 'memoryless'
description:
Audit row(s): B-42 (with D2)
Source: docs/audit/2026-10-29-dialect-0.1-narrowing-audit.md

Dialect location and rule: §6.5 'The ISA budget is (B, 0, 0, 0): reference bodies are memoryless'; the operand is steps only

Rungs blocked: 2, 4, 7, 8

Removal mechanism (0.2): Four-component budget: operand = steps; heap, stack and depth from the D2 table or the project defaults. The driver mints tokens with all four. Once D4 lifts memory and calls, every `lift.alloc` would fault FAULT_BUDGET_HEAP and every `lift.call` FAULT_BUDGET_DEPTH under the draft.

ISA 0.8 support: Yes: ISA §5.4, §10.

Why it is a narrowing / context: NS §3.1 budget row ('dynamic steps, heap bytes and recursion depth'). Top-ten narrowing #6.

title: Polyvariant cloning of device functions (BD-E-DEVICE-ADDRESS)
description:
Audit row(s): B-16
Source: docs/audit/2026-10-29-dialect-0.1-narrowing-audit.md

Dialect location and rule: §4.2 BD-E-DEVICE-ADDRESS: a host function takes the address of a device function that is not a device entry (e.g. SQLite's host-side `pVfs->xOpen = memdbOpen` while the oracle's closure contains memdbOpen)

Rungs blocked: 4

Removal mechanism (0.2): Polyvariant cloning. Device functions get device clones; host code keeps the originals. Function addresses keep their comparison-link values (NS §3.2); device code dispatches an address to the clone (O-01).

ISA 0.8 support: Yes: CC compare-and-branch (ISA §4.1).

Why it is a narrowing / context: NS §3.1 taint row ('with polyvariant specialisation when one function is used both classically and coherently'). Rung 4: SQLite built classically and queried coherently; any library used on both sides. Top-ten narrowing #10.

title: Run-time register width n (BD-E-OPERAND-UNBOUNDED on n)
description:
Audit row(s): B-07 (ISA-4)
Source: docs/audit/2026-10-29-dialect-0.1-narrowing-audit.md

Dialect location and rule: §3.4 (e.g. nbits = ceil_log2(nrows) from host input)

Rungs blocked: 4

Removal mechanism (0.2): Dispatch over a bounded candidate set when value-range analysis bounds `n` (range, known bits). In general a dynamic-width register. Rung 4 is blocked only if the demo driver takes N at run time.

ISA 0.8 support: NEEDS ISA CHANGE (ISA-4) for the general case: a dynamic-width register type in CC, `qreg[*]`, with `qreg.new cls n` taking a run-time n; region binding checks widths at the call (trap on mismatch).

Why it is a narrowing / context: NS §4.1 ('Memory is virtual ... no dynamic allocation' is a pre-VM mistake), §4.2 (real allocation).

Note: blocks rung 4 only if the demo driver takes N at run time (conditional); labelled and prioritised conservatively.

title: Oracles over several input registers, mem regions and out-parameters (oracle interface descriptor)
description:
Audit row(s): D21, B-32 (also D3, D11(b) share the redesign)
Source: docs/audit/2026-10-29-dialect-0.1-narrowing-audit.md

Dialect location and rule: §14 D21 'one input register; producers pack inputs into it'; §6.1, §6.6 BD-E-REGION-TYPE: oracle candidates must be iT (iN), 1 <= N, T <= 128

Rungs blocked: 1, 4, 7, 8

Removal mechanism (0.2): New oracle marker `__bennett_oracle_i(f, budget, iface)`, where `iface` points to a descriptor of handles (inputs, target, fault, mem regions) and classical args (provenance handles it like a table). Each parameter of the region function binds to an input register (iN <= 128), a mem region (a `ptr` parameter bound to `lift.addr` of the region base) or a classical arg. The result binds to the target; pointer out-parameters bind to further targets (<= 128-bit slices: G-15). Inputs wider than 128 bits use mem regions.

ISA 0.8 support: Yes: ISA §4.7 `(ins..)`, `(mem..)`, `(args..)`; §5.1 interface regions; §7.2 mapped regions; §3.3 region binding.

Why it is a narrowing / context: NS §4.2 (inputs preserved), NS §8 rung 4 (rowid plus database), 7 (syscall args plus snapshot), 8. Rung 1: multi-argument functions need a packing wrapper. Top-ten narrowing #2.

title: Floating point beyond binary32/64: half, bfloat, x86_fp80, fp128, transcendental intrinsics, vector FP
description:
Audit row(s): D16, B-45 (N17)
Source: docs/audit/2026-10-29-dialect-0.1-narrowing-audit.md

Dialect location and rule: §14 D16; §7.2 N17; N19 soft-float rewrite §7.3

Rungs blocked: 4, 8

Removal mechanism (0.2): (1) Vector FP: scalarise, then apply N19. (2) Transcendental intrinsics map to `bennett-arith` libm entry points (`__bennett_sf_{sin,cos,exp,log,pow,...}_fB`) with a fixed deterministic algorithm, the same one the native comparison build links. (3) half and bfloat: compute in binary32 and round (exact for + - * / sqrt since 24 >= 2p+2). x86_fp80 and fp128: `bennett-arith` soft-float.

ISA 0.8 support: Yes (integer lifted rows, CC integers).

Why it is a narrowing / context: NS §3.2 (half, bfloat, x86_fp80, fp128 are coverage-report lines until the library covers them), NS §8 rung 8 (loop-vectorised FP at O2/O3; llvm.exp/log/cos from -ffast-math or builtins). Rung 4: vector FP after O3, if present. Also rung 3+: `printf("%Lf")` (musl fmt_fp uses long double).

title: Effects: device models / virtualisation of libc calls in oracle and reversible closures
description:
Audit row(s): D11, B-17 (N half), B-51; marker list of §3.2 has no effect markers
Source: docs/audit/2026-10-29-dialect-0.1-narrowing-audit.md

Dialect location and rule: §14 D11 'F(8)'; §4.3/N18/V12; §8.6 'no external effect in 0.1'

Rungs blocked: 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8

Removal mechanism (0.2): (a) R tier: reserved runtime primitives `__bennett_dev_<model>_<op>` (or effect markers) that the plugin lowers to ISA `effect model.op`; `bennett-runtimes` musl and Julia shims implement their syscall layers on them. (b) Coherent tier: device models as lifted state: console as a buffer in lifted memory (discarded by prefix reversal unless declared output); clock as a classical arg or global initial value; entropy read from an `in` interface region (rung 8's superposed register is that region); block device and VFS as an `in` interface region holding the image (rung 4's database file) with a lifted overlay. (c) An effect with no model stays F(8) and a `trapped` coverage line: that part is L (NS §3.3).

ISA 0.8 support: Yes: R tier ISA §7.3 (console, clock, entropy, block), §4.1 `effect`; coherent tier ISA §7.2 interface regions, §3.7 pseudo-locations; host calls ISA §10 `hostcall`. New device models: ISA §17 item 3 (ISA change only for models beyond the four).

Why it is a narrowing / context: NS §3.1 effects row (marker calls on the device side for console, clock, entropy, block device), §4.2 effects table, §5 (kernel boots on the VM in the reversible tier with its devices modelled). Top-ten narrowing #3. Shares the oracle interface descriptor with D3/D21.

title: Full lifted subset in oracle regions: memory, calls, floating point, vectors (BD-E-LIFT-SUBSET)
description:
Audit row(s): D4, B-39 (and B-45 -> D16)
Source: docs/audit/2026-10-29-dialect-0.1-narrowing-audit.md

Dialect location and rule: §14 D4; §9.1 'Lifting of memory, calls, floating point and vectors in oracle regions'; §6.4.3

Rungs blocked: 1, 2, 4, 7, 8

Removal mechanism (0.2): Full lifted subset. loads, stores and GEPs -> `lift.boundscheck`/`lift.load`/`lift.store` (<= 128-bit pieces). Globals -> layout globals and data images; `lift.addr`. Escaping allocas -> `lift.alloc` at entry and `lift.free` at exit, or a shadow-stack global; non-escaping allocas -> locations. Allocator shim malloc/free -> `lift.alloc`/`lift.free`. Direct calls -> `lift.call`/`lift.ret` lprocs. Indirect calls -> O-01. FP -> soft-float bitcode from `bennett-arith`, lifted like any code. Vectors -> scalarisation before mapping (a normaliser rule). First-class aggregates -> per-field locations. Integers wider than 128 bits -> legalised into <= 128-bit limbs. Intrinsics: `*.with.overflow`, `*.sat`, bswap, ctpop, fshl/fshr, bitreverse, memcpy/memmove/memset -> expansions or runtime lprocs. Varargs -> O-03. Unwinding -> D10 transform. Pre-flight checks need the phase-1 interpreter.

ISA 0.8 support: Yes: ISA §4.2 rows `lift.load/store/alloc/free/call/ret/addr/boundscheck`; §3.7 stack and locations; §7.2 lifted memory; §16.3 example 2. Wide payloads: G-15.

Why it is a narrowing / context: NS §3.1 ('The ordinary loads and stores of lifted classical code (all of SQLite's) ... are lifted coherently'), §3.2 (soft-float; object-bounds model). Rung 1 only partially: any call left after O3 (Rust panic paths for / and %, Julia throw paths, non-inlined helpers) is outside the subset. Top-ten narrowing #1.

title: Out-of-band per-region budget tables (steps, heap, stack, depth)
description:
Audit row(s): D2 (with B-42)
Source: docs/audit/2026-10-29-dialect-0.1-narrowing-audit.md

Dialect location and rule: §14 D2 'none; B_default only'

Rungs blocked: 4, 7, 8

Removal mechanism (0.2): A driver budget table keyed by region key or content hash (§6.3), with (steps, heap, stack, depth), plus project defaults for each component. The operand budget overrides steps.

ISA 0.8 support: Yes: ISA §5.4 four-component budget; §10 `bennett_budget(steps, heap, stack, depth)`.

Why it is a narrowing / context: NS §3.1 budget row: supplied out of band by the host or driver (project-wide default, per-function table); no per-loop source annotation is ever required, so unmodified SQLite, Linux and the Monte Carlo compile as they are.

title: Classical arguments of oracle regions
description:
Audit row(s): D3 (shares the marker redesign with D21, B-32, D11(b))
Source: docs/audit/2026-10-29-dialect-0.1-narrowing-audit.md

Dialect location and rule: §14 D3 'none ... a front end specialises constants into the function'

Rungs blocked: 4, 7, 8

Removal mechanism (0.2): The oracle marker binds named parameters of the region function as classical args (read-only pseudo-locations). Run-time values come from device CC data. Part of one marker redesign: an oracle interface descriptor with inputs, targets, mem regions and args (see the D21 issue).

ISA 0.8 support: Yes: ISA §4.7 `oracle_call ... (args..)`; §5.1 `(args n: i64)`; §3.7 pseudo-locations; §9.1 `"args":[types]` (JCS spelling of types is editorial, see ISA-3).

Why it is a narrowing / context: NS §4.2 (classical inputs fixed before entry; run-time budgets and inputs from classical data); NS §8 rungs 4/7/8 ('fixed classically before entry').

title: 0.2 region-reversible-in-action candidates contradict first-operand contract
description: Example region-reversible-in-action states candidates=body. Section 1.5 says candidates is the candidate set of the first region operand. In module text order, @body calls __bennett_reversible(@classical) before @top calls __bennett_adj(@body). Expected by example: {body}; actual first region operand: {classical}. Command: python3 scripts/dialect_check.py --family recognise. Reading: module text order per section 4.1. Clarify whether candidates should select a device-entry marker, or change stated set. Checker leaves this failure visible.

title: Implement dialect 0.2 executable pre-flight checker
description: Own scripts/, spec/seeds/, spec/asm/, and corpus harness/runtime. Implement every tagged family, independent LLVM/native/ISA checks, fail-loud missing commands, family reporting, findings and progress. User job protocol forbids git commands.

title: dialect_check.py for 0.2: every example family executed; fails loudly on missing interpreter commands (codex job dialect-check-0.2)
description: Brief docs/briefs/2026-10-29-dialect-check-0.2.md. Precheck for council rounds on 0.2.

title: Dialect 0.2: rule ids without a checked example (P-1)
description: Appendix B of dialect 0.2 lists rule ids that have no example yet, so P-1 fails on them: N0, N12, N15, N25, N34, N35; V2-V16; PT12; the OUT binding's object (oracle-wide-out is recognised only, no lifted object); BLOCK, CLOCK and CONSOLE device bindings; entry-state transfer (§8.5); indirectbr (§14.9); §19.3-§19.8 driver modes; §20 platform profile. Each needs an accept/reject example with computed results before the freeze gate.

title: Checker seeds spec/seeds/ named by dialect 0.2 §21.4 do not exist
description: Dialect 0.2 §21.4 says the checker's C seeds live in spec/seeds/ (minimal allocator, shadow stack, memmove/memset/memcmp, EH state + personality subset, setjmp/longjmp, swapcontext, binary64 soft-float add/mul/cmp/conv, exp/log from musl, console/entropy stub, musl __syscall row). The 0.2 writing job verified its native= lines with scratch seeds outside the repo; spec/seeds/ was not an owned path. Create them (independent of bennett-runtimes, CLAUDE.md rule 5) so dialect_check.py can execute the native= examples.

title: Kernel and runtime platform: MMIO, interrupts, privileged state, context switch, exec, setjmp/longjmp
description:
Audit row(s): O-06 (G-16 is the efficient ISA alternative)
Source: docs/audit/2026-10-29-dialect-0.1-narrowing-audit.md

Dialect location and rule: omission: volatile accesses to device addresses become plain accesses by N9 and then memfault; no interrupts, address translation, stack switching, exec of user programs, setjmp/longjmp

Rungs blocked: 5, 6, 7

Removal mechanism (0.2): Needs a phase-2-style spike. Mechanisms without an ISA change: MMIO by address-range shims onto device models; interrupts by polling at loop back edges and function entries (deterministic timer from the clock model); context switch and setjmp/longjmp by an Asyncify-style transform (frames spilled to memory and rewound); user programs compiled as device code with a soft-MMU instrumentation of their loads and stores. Efficient alternative: ISA gap G-16.

ISA 0.8 support: Without G-16: yes, at large cost.

Why it is a narrowing / context: NS §5 (boots on the VM with its devices modelled, un-boots to the reset vector), §8 rungs 5/6/7; NS §9.11 lists setjmp as open, not excluded. Rung 6: all; rung 7: non-local exit from `panic()` to make the panic flag the payload; rung 5: Julia exceptions use sigsetjmp.

title: Oracle entry state from run-time classical state (kernel snapshot)
description:
Audit row(s): O-07 (G-12 is the efficient ISA alternative)
Source: docs/audit/2026-10-29-dialect-0.1-narrowing-audit.md

Dialect location and rule: omission: oracle memory starts as zero plus static images

Rungs blocked: 7

Removal mechanism (0.2): Rung 4: the database is a VFS file image in an `in` interface region (D11(b)); no snapshot is needed. Rung 7: a replay prologue (`lift.alloc` reproduces the CC bump addresses exactly, because ISA §4.2 `lift.alloc` and ISA §7.1 `alloc` use the same rule, max(n,1) from heap_base), then a copy of the snapshot bytes from an `in` region into globals and heap.

ISA 0.8 support: Correct in 0.8. Efficient: needs ISA gap G-12.

Why it is a narrowing / context: NS §8 rung 7 ('kernel state snapshot fixed classically after boot'); rung 4 'fixed classically before entry'. Rung 4 is only affected if the database were built in classical memory rather than as a VFS image; phase 2 should confirm.

title: Whole-program tier modes (driver mode that runs an unmodified program's entry in the R tier)
description:
Audit row(s): O-04
Source: docs/audit/2026-10-29-dialect-0.1-narrowing-audit.md

Dialect location and rule: omission: an unmodified program has no markers, so nothing enters the R tier; NS §4.2 names `__bennett_reversible` or a driver mode; §11.3 has no such option

Rungs blocked: 3, 5, 6

Removal mechanism (0.2): Driver option `-bennett-tier=reversible -bennett-entry=<sym>`: the entry is treated as a `reversible` region over the whole program with argv/env from the launch. Un-run is whole-run reversal; tape replay through the effect tape.

ISA 0.8 support: Yes: ISA §10 `bennett_run`, `bennett_reverse`, reverse eligibility; ISA §7.3/§7.4.

Why it is a narrowing / context: NS §4.2 effects table (reversible row), NS §5 (the kernel compiles, boots on the VM in the reversible tier), NS §8 rungs 3/5/6. Top-ten narrowing #7.

title: Inline asm and target intrinsics classification (lowered / shimmed / trapped)
description:
Audit row(s): O-02
Source: docs/audit/2026-10-29-dialect-0.1-narrowing-audit.md

Dialect location and rule: omission: not mentioned in the dialect

Rungs blocked: 3, 6, 7

Removal mechanism (0.2): A per-target classification table in the dialect (asm string + constraints -> lowered: e.g. empty asm with a `memory` clobber -> no-op, `pause` -> no-op; shimmed: `syscall` -> the `bennett-runtimes` syscall entry, `rdtsc` -> clock model; trapped: everything else, F(8)), plus a table for target intrinsics (`llvm.x86.*`).

ISA 0.8 support: Yes: CC/R code, `effect` (ISA §7.3).

Why it is a narrowing / context: NS §3.3: target intrinsics and asm are classified lowered / trapped / shimmed in the coverage report. Rung 3: musl `__syscall` is inline asm; rungs 6, 7: kernel.

title: Storing handles through pointers loaded from memory or returned by functions (collections of handles)
description:
Audit row(s): B-24 (BD-E-HANDLE-STORE, B5, BD-E-HANDLE-UNTRACKED); same points-to mechanism as D9, B-26, B-27, B-29, B-33
Source: docs/audit/2026-10-29-dialect-0.1-narrowing-audit.md

Dialect location and rule: §5.2 r5; Rust `Vec<Handle>::push` and C++ `std::vector<bennett_q>` store through a buffer pointer loaded from the vector header and are rejected

Rungs blocked: none directly

Removal mechanism (0.2): Replace bases with a whole-program, field-sensitive points-to analysis over device functions (Andersen-style; allocation sites as in D9; pointer slots tracked through memory as C3 already does for regions; call results through `ret` operands as P9 does). Reject only stores whose target may be host-visible memory (EXT, or memory D25 copies out). For residual imprecision use a run-time check at markers (`T-DEAD`), which §5.2 already relies on.

ISA 0.8 support: Run-time-sized tables need ISA-4/ISA-5.

Why it is a narrowing / context: NS §3.1 handle row: 'Collections of handles are supported through a handle table'; only a handle at a superposed address is rejected. Blocks Rust, C++ and Julia quantum code with collections; no rung. Top-ten narrowing #9.

title: Links mixing LLVM majors
description:
Audit row(s): D19, B-53
Source: docs/audit/2026-10-29-dialect-0.1-narrowing-audit.md

Dialect location and rule: §14 D19; §11.1 'one major per link'

Rungs blocked: 5

Removal mechanism (0.2): Read all bitcode with the newest major in the envelope (bitcode is backward-readable) and run that major's plugin. Publish the tested pairs; build `bennett-runtimes`/`bennett-arith` bitcode per major.

ISA 0.8 support: n/a.

Why it is a narrowing / context: NS §3.2: a mixed-language link (bitcode from different LLVM majors) is supported within a tested compatibility envelope. Rung 5: Julia's LLVM major against runtime bitcode; mixed-language programs.

title: Exceptions and unwinding in the device closure (invoke/landingpad, Rust panics, C++ throw)
description:
Audit row(s): D10, B-12
Source: docs/audit/2026-10-29-dialect-0.1-narrowing-audit.md

Dialect location and rule: §14 D10; §3.7 BD-E-EH, except marker invokes

Rungs blocked: 1

Removal mechanism (0.2): Explicit-propagation transform on device functions: every function gets an unwinding flag in its return; `invoke` becomes call + test + branch to the landing pad; `resume` and the runtime raise primitives (`_Unwind_RaiseException`, `__cxa_throw`, `__rust_start_panic`) become a return with the flag set. Catch matching uses typeinfo identity through the shim personality. Unwinding out of a region gives fault code 4 (a dedicated ISA code is optional).

ISA 0.8 support: Yes: CC multi-result `call`/`ret` (ISA §4.1); lifted `lift.call`/`lift.ret` with the flag in a location; `fault` (ISA §4.2).

Why it is a narrowing / context: NS §3.1 control row: exceptions and unwinding inside a region are step-machine control flow where the handler is in the region, and a fault code where it is not. Rust code with cleanups (rung 1), C++/Rust device code in general.

title: Taint-driven lifting of classical code under ctrl/adj/compute (coherent lifting; R1)
description:
Audit row(s): 1.4-d, D17, B-31, B-50, O-05 (all same mechanism); audit §3 TDL-1..TDL-10
Source: docs/audit/2026-10-29-dialect-0.1-narrowing-audit.md

Dialect location and rule: §1.4(d), §6.1 'region kind fixed by the marker', §6.6 'plugin never outlines', §8.4 (classical code of ctrl/adj/compute bodies runs once, classically), §14 D17

Rungs blocked: none directly

Removal mechanism (0.2): see audit

ISA 0.8 support: Not a dedicated ISA change. Yes: ISA §5.3 (action bodies call oracles), §4.7 `ctl w <call>` and `(args..)`, §3.3 region binding, §5.2 oracle is an involution. Efficiency items: G-13, G-14, G-15.

Why it is a narrowing / context: Does not block rungs 4/7/8 (they use the explicit `oracle` marker once D4, D21/D3, D11, B-42, O-01 are removed). Blocks NS §0 ('controlled-anything ... everything else is inferred') and the NS §5 REPL scene `when(q) do f(x) end`. Under the draft, classical stores of a ctrl body happen on both branches of q: a different result, not just a rejection. O-05 (coherent memory after a region) is part of this (TDL-4, TDL-2).


Taint-driven lifting (TDL), specifiable as dialect 0.2 rules (audit §3.2; ISA 0.8 permits it, no ISA change needed):
- TDL-1 Interface vs body. The marker fixes the region's interface (action for ctrl/adj/compute, oracle for oracle/inplace). The body is partitioned by content (TDL-3), never rejected for containing classical code (NS §4.2).
- TDL-2 Coherence lattice Cl below Co over values and (field-sensitive) abstract objects, flow-sensitive. Seeds: a store during generation of an action region to an object live after the invocation makes it Co from region exit (promotion); a load from a Co object is Co. Propagation: data dependence; control dependence (Co branch makes dependents Co, stores predicated); memory (store of Co value or under Co control makes the object Co). Interprocedural, context-sensitive, polyvariant clones per coherence signature (NS §3.1).
- TDL-3 Partition. G (generation) = Cl instructions not control-dependent on a Co branch whose stores target Cl or non-escaping objects; runs once in CC as today. Each maximal single-entry single-exit region of Co instructions is outlined (CodeExtractor) into O_k: Cl live-ins become classical args, Co live-ins input registers, Co objects read the arena region (in), Co live-outs and written bytes output targets. O_k is lifted by the D4 map; irreducible coherent code is outlined as a whole function.
- TDL-4 Coherent arena: every object that may become Co is allocated in a static range [A_coh, A_coh+2^A) of the layout, inside every oracle's [0,2^H) and disjoint from CC globals/heap (ISA §7.1/§7.2; G-13 would lift the restriction); contents in a CC-held qreg[8*2^A] bound to region[A,8] (ISA §3.3). The bennett-runtimes coherent allocator keeps bookkeeping classically; a still-Cl arena object has a CC shadow, G-code stores mirrored as basis-state updates. After promotion, CC reads of the object are a compile-time error BD-E-TAINT-HOST (host-visible outputs leave only through measurement).
- TDL-5 Events. Case A: a G store to an escaping object with classical old and new contents appends `xmask o, old^new`. Case B: each dynamic entry into slice O_k appends `oracle O_k` (args = Cl live-ins, ins = Co live-in registers, mem = arena, tgt = fresh registers for Co live-outs and new byte contents, fr = fresh wire[4]) then exchange events (`qexch` on slices for classical addresses, `qexchm` for Co addresses, ISA §4.6). Outputs wider than 128 bits are sliced (G-15).
- TDL-6 Control and adjoint: ctrl adds the control wire to every event (`ctl w`, ISA §4.7); oracle_call, qexch, qexchm and X are self-adjoint (ISA §5.3). adj of a region with escaping writes consumes the history registers of its forward invocation; without them the adjoint of a non-injective update does not exist (that case is L: NS §4.2 requires an action to be a unitary on its declared wires).
- TDL-7 History: displaced contents, per-slice fault wires, Co temporaries; lives in declared mutable wires; freed when the scheduler chooses (NS §3.1 garbage row); `compute(f, use)` frees it through adjoint(E_f). Memory is versioned, never overwritten.
- TDL-8 Faults: a final combine oracle XORs the first nonzero per-slice code into the region's declared fault register (lifted select chain).
- TDL-9 Budget: the ctrl operand or the D2 table gives (steps, heap, stack, depth) for every O_k token; exhaustion is that slice's FAULT_BUDGET_* reaching the region fault.
- TDL-10 Co control of quantum operations: a marker call control-dependent on a Co branch or with Co index/op code: an oracle computes the condition into a fresh wire and the gate is issued under `qpred` once per candidate (ISA §3.5, §4.6). A Co angle is predicated per candidate when finite, else rejected (L: NS promises predication, not superposed parameters). A Co trip count of a gate-issuing loop is padded to the budget bound, unrolled in the event list, per-iteration flags kept as history; G-14 would replace that with an action step machine.

ISA gaps: G-13 (dynamic region base), G-14 (action step machine), G-15 (wide oracle payloads) are efficiency items for ISA 0.9. ISA-4 matters for adj of a generation whose register set is known only at run time (record the event trace with its registers and replay in reverse). R1 is a dialect design task for phase 3 with no ISA blocker.

title: dialect 0.2: remove every narrowing of dialect 0.1
description:
Standing rule (bennett/docs/plan/2026-10-29-path-to-north-star.md): no narrowing of north-star scope of any kind. A deferral may postpone mechanics while keeping the capability; a default of reject/refuse/none/fault for something the north star promises is a narrowing.

Source: docs/audit/2026-10-29-dialect-0.1-narrowing-audit.md (phase 0, commit 3bb2ae2). 96 rows classified: N 57, M 12, L 27. 17 N rows only point at another row's mechanism, leaving 40 distinct narrowings (incl. 7 omissions O-01..O-07; O-05 is folded into the taint-driven lifting issue). Each is a child issue of this epic, labelled `narrowing` and `blocks-rung-N`.

Rungs (NS §8): 1 scalar functions; 2 pointers/structs/byte memory; 3 musl hello world; 4 Grover over SQLite; 5 Julia on a shim runtime; 6 xv6 and Linux in the reversible tier; 7 kernel fuzzing; 8 Monte Carlo amplitude estimation. Priority 0 = blocks rung 4.

Notes for the 0.2 editor (audit §4): the pre-flight checker only executes the scalar subset, so every removal needs the phase-1 reference interpreter for its checked examples. B-24, B-26, B-27, B-29, B-33 (and D9) share one whole-program field-sensitive points-to analysis; specify it once. D21, D3, B-32 and D11(b) share one oracle interface descriptor; specify it once. Before 0.2 freezes, phase 2 (SQLite) should confirm the VFS-image route needs neither G-12 nor ISA-11 for rung 4.

title: Handles across the host-device boundary (device-entry parameters and results of handle type)
description:
Audit row(s): B-30
Source: docs/audit/2026-10-29-dialect-0.1-narrowing-audit.md

Dialect location and rule: §5.4, §8.5 T-LEAK at device-entry return: registers never outlive a device-entry call

Rungs blocked: none directly

Removal mechanism (0.2): Device-entry parameters and results of handle type map to launch `QREG` arguments and results. On the host they are opaque 64-bit register ids that host code may copy and store but never dereference or compute on (checked by extending provenance to host functions for these values). Leak checking moves to program end or `bennett_qreg_free`.

ISA 0.8 support: Yes: ISA §10 `BENNETT_ARG_QREG`, results of kind QREG, `bennett_qreg_free`; ISA §3.3 'Host-supplied register ids are qreg values'.

Why it is a narrowing / context: NS §5 REPL (quantum registers are REPL values with lexical lifetime); NS §4.4 launch ABI. Blocks the REPL scene and Bennett.jl; no rung.

title: Handle equality and null comparison (icmp eq/ne on a handle; `if (!q)`, Rust Option niche)
description:
Audit row(s): D8, B-19
Source: docs/audit/2026-10-29-dialect-0.1-narrowing-audit.md

Dialect location and rule: §14 D8; §5.2 r1 'icmp/switch on a handle' rejected

Rungs blocked: none directly

Removal mechanism (0.2): DECIDED 2026-10-29 by the maintainer's no-narrowing rule: supported in 0.2. Define `icmp eq`/`ne` of a handle against `null` or another handle as identity (a live handle is never null; two handles are equal iff they are the same register). The result is not handle-derived. Rust's `Option<Handle>` null-niche tests and C's `if (!q)` both produce this. Maintainer decision 2 forbids comparison of handle-derived *integers*; `icmp` on the `ptr` handle is not covered by it.

ISA 0.8 support: Yes: CC `icmp` on register-id integers (the dialect's representation of handles in CC).

Why it is a narrowing / context: NS §3.1 handle row; NS §0 (unmodified C/Rust idioms). Without it Rust/C++ programs holding handles break. Blocks no rung.

Removal mechanism (0.2): (1) Remove T-BORROW: outside a generation `qborrow` is a clean allocation (sound, since a correct borrow user also works on clean wires). (2) Inside statically compilable generations, lower to ISA `qborrow`/`qreturn` with borrow-frame verification (translation lemma, or a T3 claim).

ISA 0.8 support: Inside actions: yes, ISA §4.3, §5.6, §9.4. In CC: ISA-9 (real gap, not blocking; clean allocation is the fallback).

Why it is a narrowing / context: NS §3.1 allocate (clean / dirty ...), §4.3 dirty borrowing as a first-class resource.
